title: The Homecoming of Westbrook High
premise: Westbrook High sits atop the sealed foundations of a defunct conservatory, and every generation the school's elite 'Choir' selects one student to inherit a power that keeps the building — and the town — standing, at a terrible price. When Kestrel Joubert's only friend Marisol vanishes leaving behind a ring of old keys, Kestrel is pulled into a hidden competition disguised as the spring championship season: win the state title to earn an audience with the Choir, then survive the final audition beneath the gymnasium. Kestrel learns Marisol refused the inheritance and was taken below; in the end, Kestrel wins both championships but shatters the Choir's cycle by opening the sealed doors, freeing Marisol and the generations kept before her, and choosing belonging on their own terms rather than the school's.
about_author: Oscar Dunmore is the pen name of a former substitute teacher who spent two years in a small mill town and never stopped wondering what the high school was built over. They write stories about kids who refuse to be background characters in other people's institutions.

chapters.title: Counting Days
chapters.summary: Kestrel Joubert's POV. Three months from graduation, Kestrel maps Westbrook High's exits and social strata, determined to stay invisible until June. Establishes Marisol Vega as the one person who sees them. Emotional beat: weary self-protection cracked open by genuine friendship.

chapters.title: The Keys Under the Bleachers
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Marisol misses their lunch ritual, then a week of classes. In her locker: seven tarnished keys on a ribbon and a note reading 'Don't audition.' The school administration acts strangely unconcerned. Emotional beat: dread blooming where annoyance should be.

chapters.title: Everyone Knows Everyone
chapters.summary: Alternating Kestrel and Marisol's diary fragments. Kestrel canvasses classmates and finds eerie uniformity: everyone praises the Choir, the school's student leadership, and no one remembers Marisol clearly. Emotional beat: the horror of being edited out of collective memory.

chapters.title: Tryouts Are Mandatory
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Coach Ambrose 'encourages' Kestrel onto the track team, noting the championship roster feeds directly into Choir selection. First glimpse of golden-boy captain Theo Ashford, whose charm has teeth. Emotional beat: resentment curdling into reluctant ambition.

chapters.title: What the Building Remembers
chapters.summary: Marisol's diary, dated before her disappearance. She describes finding the old conservatory blueprints and hearing music through the gym floor at night. Kestrel reads it alone in the library stacks. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: The First Key
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The smallest key opens a maintenance hatch revealing a stairwell that shouldn't exist, warm air rising from below. Theo catches them there — and instead of reporting it, offers alliance. Emotional beat: suspicion wrestling with loneliness.

chapters.title: Relays and Rehearsals
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Training montage interwoven with Choir rituals: seniors whispering pledges, Principal Wren watching everything. Theo reveals he's next in line for inheritance and hates it. Emotional beat: two rivals discovering they're both prisoners.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Graduated Twice
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Research uncovers a 1974 yearbook photo of a girl identical to the current Choir president, Odile Marsh. Every few decades, someone doesn't age out. Emotional beat: vertigo — the pattern is older and larger than imagined.

chapters.title: Homecoming Is a Promise
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The town's obsessive homecoming tradition is revealed as a renewal ceremony; alumni return not to visit but to be remembered into the walls. Kestrel's mother, an alumna, goes glassy-eyed at the mention. Emotional beat: betrayal by the people who should protect you.

chapters.title: Second Key, Broken Lock
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A key opens the band room's false wall; inside, decades of confiscated trophies and a choir robe embroidered with Marisol's name, already waiting. Someone expected her to join. Emotional beat: cold certainty that she was chosen, not lost.

chapters.title: The Price of Winning
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo confesses the inheritance terms: the champion gains power over the school but becomes bound to it forever, sustaining the seal with their own years. His father won in 1989 and hasn't aged since. Emotional beat: pity for the gilded cage.

chapters.title: Losing on Purpose
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel tries to throw a qualifying meet to escape selection, but losing triggers the alternate clause — the runner-up is taken first. The system punishes refusal. Emotional beat: rage at a game rigged in every direction.

chapters.title: Odile Offers Tea
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Odile Marsh recruits Kestrel gently, promising Marisol is 'in rehearsal below' and can be freed if Kestrel simply wins and takes the mantle instead. The offer is sincere, which makes it worse. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a kind face.

chapters.title: The Third Through Fifth Keys
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A night expedition unlocks three more doors: classrooms frozen mid-lesson, students from 1952 still seated, aware but dimmed. One whispers 'don't sing along.' Emotional beat: compassion hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Where Loyalty Ends
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo must choose between warning the Choir about Kestrel's break-ins or covering for them. He burns his own pledge card. Emotional beat: loyalty redefined — protecting a person over an institution.

chapters.title: State Championship
chapters.summary: Full cast. The meet itself: Kestrel runs the anchor leg with the whole town chanting, wins the title, and is immediately summoned to the 'post-game reception' below. Emotional beat: triumph laced with terror — winning was the trap all along.

chapters.title: The Final Audition
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Beneath the gym, the Choir performs the binding song; Kestrel, holding the last keys, must sing the acceptance verse. Instead they find Marisol among the dimmed chorus and begin unlocking chains mid-song. Emotional beat: defiance as performance.

chapters.title: Everything the Walls Hold
chapters.summary: Climax. The seal fights back — the building groans, memories flood, Odile begs Kestrel to finish or everyone fades. Theo joins his voice to Kestrel's off-key refusal, breaking harmony. The doors blow open. Emotional beat: chaos, sacrifice, and the sound of something old letting go.

chapters.title: Morning Roll Call
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Dawn: the missing generations wake confused but free; some choose to stay and finally graduate properly. Odile, unbound, ages years in minutes and thanks them through tears. Emotional beat: exhausted, imperfect grace.

chapters.title: What Marisol Chose
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Reunited, Marisol admits she ran because she feared Kestrel would follow her down. They argue, laugh, and agree the friendship survives truth better than silence. Emotional beat: repair without erasure.

chapters.title: Graduation Day
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. No more counting days. Kestrel walks the stage in a gym that feels merely like a gym, Theo beside them, keys donated to the town historical society. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: Epilogue: The Empty Stairwell
chapters.summary: Distant third person, years later. Demolition crews find nothing beneath the foundations but clean earth and a child's ribbon holding seven keys. Somewhere, a new school hums faintly. Emotional beat: hopeful vigilance — freedom is maintained, not owned.
